array_aliasing.quote: It prints 1 9; The line b = a makes b a copy of a; so b is a separate array; Changing b[0] to 9 only changes b, and a[0] is still 1
array_aliasing.rule: wrong rule: Assigning an array reference copies the array. Right rule: b = a; copies only the reference, so a and b refer to the same array and b[i] = v also changes a[i].

paths.label: shown
paths.quote: It prints 1 9; The line b = a makes b a copy of a; so b is a separate array; Changing b[0] to 9 only changes b, and a[0] is still 1
paths.logic: Folk meaning: in maths and English, 'b = a' means b becomes an equal but independent copy, and 'a == b' means 'have the same values'. Java rule: for arrays, b = a copies only the reference, so both names denote one array, and == tests whether two names refer to the same array.

paths.label: correct
paths.quote: It prints 1 9; Changing b[0] to 9 only changes b, and a[0] is still 1
paths.logic: The first element of a is a[1].
paths.twin_logic: Numbering begins with 0; the first element is a[0].

paths.label: confirmed
paths.logic: When one operand of + is a String, Java converts the other operand to a String before concatenating.

paths.label: shown
paths.logic: Evaluate + operators left to right (same precedence, left-associative): at each +, if either current operand is a String, convert the other and concatenate; otherwise add numerically. Parenthesized parts are evaluated first.
